summary: The Federal Lands Amplified Security for the Homeland Act (FLASH Act) addresses public safety and environmental issues on federal lands along the southern border. The bill requires the construction of navigable roads and deployment of security technology, permits U.S. Customs and Border Protection to access wilderness areas, allows border states to place temporary barriers on federal lands without special authorizations, mandates initiatives to clean up trash and illegal cannabis cultivation sites, establishes a fuels management initiative to reduce wildfire risks, and prohibits the use of federal funds to house certain aliens on federal lands, explicitly revoking a lease at Floyd Bennett Field in New York.

affected_groups.effect: Granted expanded access to federal and wilderness lands, new navigable roads, security infrastructure, and explicit protections from agency interference to conduct enforcement and search and rescue.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Department of Defense personnel

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to place temporary security structures on covered federal lands for up to one year without needing a special use authorization.

Subject to increased criminal fines and penalties for violating fire and sanitation regulations or engaging in illegal cannabis cultivation with improper pesticides on federal land, and prohibited from being housed on federal land management agency properties.
affected_groups.group: Aliens without lawful immigration status / specified aliens

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary concerned to construct and maintain at least 584 miles of navigable roads and deploy security technology on covered federal lands along the southern border within 5 years.

Authorizes the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to conduct search and rescue operations, use motor vehicles and aircraft, and construct roads and physical barriers within wilderness areas.
Allows a Border State to place movable, temporary structures on covered federal lands for up to 1 year without a special use authorization, provided 45 days notice is given.
Prohibits the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture from impeding, prohibiting, or restricting CBP activities on covered federal lands within 100 miles of the southern border.

Establishes Trespass Cannabis Cultivation Site Response Initiatives and authorizes $16,037,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2032 for remediation, alongside increased criminal penalties for illegal pesticide application and cannabis cultivation.
Establishes the Southern Border Fuels Management Initiative under the Secretary of the Interior with an authorization of $3,660,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2032.
Prohibits the use of federal funds to provide housing to specified aliens on lands managed by federal land management agencies and revokes the lease for alien housing at Floyd Bennett Field.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Federal Lands Amplified Security for the Homeland Act (FLASH Act) addresses public safety and environmental issues on federal lands along the southern border. The bill requires the construction of navigable roads and deployment of security technology, permits U.S. Customs and Border Protection to access wilderness areas, allows border states to place temporary barriers on federal lands without special authorizations, mandates initiatives to clean up trash and illegal cannabis cultivation sites, establishes a fuels management initiative to reduce wildfire risks, and prohibits the use of federal funds to house certain aliens on federal lands, explicitly revoking a lease at Floyd Bennett Field in New York.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping policy shift regarding the management of federal public lands along the southern border, prioritizing border enforcement, infrastructure development, and environmental remediation over standard wilderness and public land restrictions. It directly affects federal land use policies, immigration enforcement funding, environmental cleanup operations, and specific federal leases.
